transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

The 'U' code on Beko induction hobs typically means it cannot detect a suitable pan. This is very often due to the cookware itself rather than a fault with the new hob. Induction zones only heat magnetic pans (usually cast iron or certain stainless steels) that are flat and large enough to cover the zone. Please try these two quick checks:
1. Test your saucepan: Place a fridge magnet on the base of the pan. If it does not stick firmly, the hob will not heat it. Try a different pan you know works elsewhere.
2. Check for locks: Ensure no child-lock or control lock is active (often indicated by a key or padlock symbol). If the magnet sticks and no lock is on, but it still flashes 'U' with that specific pan, let me know exactly which pan you are using.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

I tried the magnet: it doesn't stick to my saucepans, but it does stick to my cast-iron casserole, and that one heated fine. No child lock on as far as I can tell, other buttons work. So is the hob OK and it's just my pans?!

Yes, your hob is perfectly fine. The 'U' code suggests it cannot detect a suitable pan, and since the magnet test showed your saucepans are not magnetic while your cast-iron casserole worked, the issue is most likely the cookware. Induction hobs only heat pans that have a magnetic base (usually cast iron or specific stainless steels). You will need to use compatible pans for those zones.
